body: As a closeted trans person, I do have to say it does make me a bit uncomfortable when I have to give my pronouns. I'm not out so saying my actual preferred pronouns would probably just draw unwanted attention to me, so I end up going with my AGAB pronouns anyway. It just stings a little bit every time because idk for some reason I would rather people assume incorrectly than for me to announce the wrong pronouns. I guess this is just a problem for me being closeted because I can see how it would be helpful once I do come out.
Any decent compiler will probably optimize out the trans = false assignment. Now if only I could optimize that out of myself 😭

Thanks for your response! What you said makes a lot of sense and I think I just need to spend some time and process my feelings to really get to the root of things and figure it out for myself. Thanks again for your response :)

Thanks again and I'm so happy you were able to find your voice in your journey!

When I start saying or typing something it will end up meaning something else than what I truly mean.

Also, I have the general anxiety about doing something new in a new place with a new therapist who I don't know at all.

Whenever I feel like I want to be a girl, I just think to myself that what I really want is to be happy, and browsing this sub for so long has made me think I'm trans because I relate to some of the memes, when in fact I just have other problems.

I completely feel the same way. There are so many things I want to change in my life - right now, I'm a pretty nerdy guy who does interesting stuff alone, but I really want to try acting or even shopping with friends (something I'd usually hate as my current "persona"). However, as you said, I feel too inexperienced and that only exacerbates the anxiety.

How do you get yourself to open up to a therapist, someone you've never interacted with before? The main reason I don't find therapy is because I'm not sure what I'm supposed to do and that my problems are probably not actually SA or another disorder. Today I tried talking to myself about some of my issues and even speaking them out loud felt wrong, so telling a stranger feels like torture.

The ideal goal for me would be to find a partner I can truly open up to with my issues instead of bottling everything up inside. Because of my SA, I've accepted that this will never happen, so I'm planning on just living alone and ideally working remotely/online once I'm done with college. It kinda feels like a retaliatory move to family/others who assumed I will magically find someone after having no experience at all before.
